::: {#rem-cross-entropy-loss}
#### Why models are fit by minimizing cross-entropy

Fitting a classifier by minimizing cross-entropy
chooses the model's distribution $q$
so that a code built for $q$ would spend as few bits as possible
on the observed labels.
By @rem-cross-entropy-wrong-code, that pushes $q$
toward the distribution the labels came from.

For a single labeled example,
let $e$ be the distribution that puts all its mass on the observed label.
Then $H_2(e) = 0$
([as for a coin that always lands heads](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#exm-entropy-coin)),
so the example's cross-entropy loss $H_2(e, q)$ equals $D_2(e \,\|\, q)$:
every bit the loss reports is a wasted one.

:::
